Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the InnovaTech Solutions Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Sarah Jones, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jones, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to InnovaTech Solutions’ earnings call. Joining me today are Michael Chen, CEO; David Lee, CFO; Emily Carter, COO; and John Williams, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Michael Chen.

Michael Chen, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Sarah. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, our customer LTA portfolio continues to be a key driver of our long-term success. We're confident in our ability to continue growing this portfolio, managing underutilization risks effectively, and delivering exceptional value to our customers. This reflects a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by the positive aspects of the amended LTA and the overall growth of our LTA portfolio.

We also continued to drive improvements through key capability launches tied to our "Project Nightingale" initiative focused on optimizing power efficiency in our mobile processors. This initiative supports broader adoption and has further boosted ASP due to improved battery life and thermal performance.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our gross margin results, where we’ve seen a significant improvement. Our adjusted gross margin for the quarter reached 29.9%, a substantial 12 percentage point improvement compared to Q3 2023.

Now I’ll hand it over to David Lee to discuss the financials in greater detail.

David Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Michael, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our sales by segment or platforms, their respective margin levels, and their respective management comments has contributed meaningfully to our overall performance. We achieved overall revenue of $4.8 billion for the quarter, representing a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion.

Second, we saw positive contribution from our net margin and Diluted EPS results, which landed at 16% and $0.67, respectively. This dramatic increase is primarily attributable to a confluence of factors, including revenue growth and cost optimization.

And although still early, our P&L guidance for next quarter is projecting total revenue to land between $2.05 billion and $2.1 billion. We also project adjusted gross profit to range from $595 million to $630 million.

With that, I’ll turn it to Emily Carter for a deeper look at operational performance.

Emily Carter, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, David.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was the continued growth in our customer LTA portfolio, particularly in the APAC region. We signed a major LTA with "GreenTech Solutions Ltd." in Singapore, securing a $750 million commitment over the next 7 years.

Additionally, our net margin and Diluted EPS results have enabled more investment in R&D to develop innovative new products and enhance our existing offerings. We are particularly focused on leveraging AI and machine learning to create solutions that address the evolving needs of our customers.

We’re also seeing early traction in our CapEx investments, where updated processes and strategic alignment with our focus on innovation and delivering cutting-edge services to our customers. By investing in AI, ML, and other emerging technologies, we are positioning ourselves to be a leader in the next wave of digital transformation.

Now I’ll pass it to John Williams for the tech and product update.

John Williams, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Emily.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to "Project Nightingale", supporting broader adoption and further boosting ASP due to improved battery life and thermal performance.

We’ve also supported our P&L guidance for next quarter, and we are actively engaged with several leading automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers, securing long-term contracts that provide excellent revenue visibility.

And finally, on our CapEx investments, our new architecture is enabling us to capture a larger share of the rapidly growing cloud market.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the gross margin results and whether you anticipate further improvements in the coming quarters?

Michael Chen:
Certainly. The 12 percentage point year-over-year improvement is a testament to the multifaceted strategies we've implemented over the past year. Breaking down this improvement, approximately 80%, or 9.6 percentage points, can be attributed to both increased Average Selling Prices (ASPs) and a favorable product mix. The remaining 20%, or 2.4 percentage points, stems from higher production volumes, leading to better fixed-cost absorption. We believe that by executing on these strategies, we can continue to deliver strong gross margin performance and drive sustainable, profitable growth.

Analyst 2:
On sales by segment, how much of your revenue is attributed to the automotive segment, and what are your expectations for growth in that sector?

David Lee:
The automotive market contributed approximately 5% to our total Q3 revenue, or roughly $240 million. While representing a smaller portion of our overall revenue, this segment is strategically important for our long-term growth. We are experiencing strong traction in the electric vehicle (EV) market, particularly in China and Europe, where government incentives and consumer demand are driving rapid adoption. We are committed to investing in this area and becoming a leading provider of automotive semiconductor solutions.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to "Project Nightingale"?

John Williams:
"Project Nightingale" is a new initiative focused on optimizing power efficiency in our mobile processors. We've rolled it out to our Apex series processors, which has further boosted ASP due to improved battery life and thermal performance. We're seeing significant adoption in the Asia-Pacific region, especially in emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia.

Analyst 4:
And finally, on CapEx, is this level of spending sustainable, and how will it impact future profitability?

Emily Carter:
While the current CapEx spending may appear high relative to revenue, it is important to recognize that these investments are essential for supporting our long-term growth strategy. We are building a robust and scalable infrastructure that will enable us to capture a larger share of the rapidly growing cloud market. We believe that these CapEx investments will generate significant returns in the long run by driving revenue growth, improving profitability, and enhancing our competitive position.

Closing

Michael Chen:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
